questions.stem: A musician composes and records an original song. Which form of intellectual property automatically protects the song against unauthorised copying?
questions.explanation: Creative works such as songs, books, paintings and software code are protected by copyright from the moment they are created. A patent protects inventions, a trademark protects names and logos that identify a brand, and a domain name is only an address on the Internet.

optionRationale.1: A patent is meant for new inventions and processes, not for a creative work such as a song.
optionRationale.3: A trademark protects the symbol or name that identifies a business, not the song itself.
optionRationale.4: A domain name is an Internet address and gives no protection to a creative work.

questions.objective: Match a creative work with copyright

questions.stem: A company hands over 40 old but working laptops to a village school instead of discarding them. In the management of e-waste, this action is called
questions.explanation: Passing on equipment that still works so that another person can use it as it is, is reuse. It keeps the product out of the waste stream. Recycling breaks the product down to recover its materials, while incineration and landfilling are disposal methods that harm the environment.

optionRationale.1: Recycling means dismantling the machines to recover metals and plastics, which is not done here.
optionRationale.2: Incineration means burning waste, which would release toxic fumes and is not what the company did.
optionRationale.3: Landfilling means burying waste in the ground, but these laptops are still being used.

questions.objective: Identify reuse as an e-waste management method

questions.stem: Without Meena's knowledge, a person uses her Aadhaar number and photograph to apply for a loan in her name. This act is best described as
questions.explanation: Using another person's personal details, such as an identity number and photograph, to pretend to be that person and gain money or benefits is identity theft. Plagiarism concerns copied work, cyber bullying concerns hurtful messages, and software piracy concerns illegal copying of programs.

optionRationale.1: Plagiarism means passing off someone else's written work as your own, not misusing identity details.
optionRationale.2: Cyber bullying means harassing a person through repeated hurtful online messages, which did not happen here.
optionRationale.4: Software piracy means unauthorised copying or use of software, not the misuse of a person's identity.

questions.stem: A student downloads a photograph licensed as CC BY-ND, crops it, changes its colours, and posts the edited picture on her blog with a note crediting the photographer. The use is not for money. Which licence condition is she breaking?
options: Attribution, because she did not name the photographer
NonCommercial, because blogs are always meant for earning money
NoDerivatives, because an edited picture is a modified version of the work
ShareAlike, because she did not licence the edited picture in the same way
questions.explanation: BY-ND lets others copy and share the work with credit, but only in its original, unchanged form. Cropping and recolouring creates a derivative work, so the NoDerivatives condition is broken. Credit was given, so Attribution is satisfied, and the use is not commercial.

optionRationale.1: She did credit the photographer, so the Attribution condition is satisfied.
optionRationale.2: The use is stated to be non-commercial, so a NonCommercial condition is not broken (and this licence has none).
optionRationale.4: ShareAlike is not a condition of the BY-ND licence, so it cannot be broken.

questions.objective: Apply the NoDerivatives condition of Creative Commons

questions.stem: Which of the following is a good practice of netiquette while writing a formal e-mail to a teacher?
options: Writing a clear subject line and closing with a polite greeting
Typing the whole message in capital letters so that it gets noticed
Forwarding a private mail of a classmate to the whole class for fun
Using only short-hand chat words and many emoticons in the message
questions.explanation: Good netiquette means being polite, clear and respectful. A meaningful subject and a courteous closing help the reader. Capital letters read as shouting, forwarding private mail breaches privacy, and slang is not suitable in a formal message to a teacher.

optionRationale.2: Capital letters are read as shouting and are considered rude.
optionRationale.3: Forwarding a private message without permission is a breach of privacy.
optionRationale.4: Chat short-hand and emoticons are not suitable for a formal mail.

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements.
A. Ransomware locks or encrypts the files of a user and demands money to unlock them.
B. Spam means unwanted bulk messages sent to many people.
C. A trademark protects a new invention for a limited period.
D. Copying and using a paid software without paying for it is software piracy.
Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: A, B and D are correct definitions of ransomware, spam and software piracy. C is false because it is a patent, not a trademark, that protects an invention for a limited period; a trademark protects a name, logo or symbol that identifies a product or company.

optionRationale.1: C is false, so any pair or group containing C is wrong, and B and D are true as well.
optionRationale.3: C is false, so this option wrongly includes it and also leaves out the true statement A.
optionRationale.4: C is false, so this option is wrong and also leaves out the true statement D.

questions.objective: Judge statements about cyber crimes and intellectual property

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): A trademark gives its owner exclusive rights over a new invention.
Reason (R): A patent gives the inventor exclusive rights over an invention for a limited period.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: Exclusive rights over a new invention are given by a patent, not by a trademark, so the assertion is false. A trademark protects a name, logo or symbol that identifies a brand. The reason correctly states what a patent does, so R is true.

optionRationale.1: A is false, so the pair cannot be a true assertion with a true explanation.
optionRationale.2: A is false because a trademark does not protect an invention, so both cannot be true.
optionRationale.3: R is true, since a patent really gives the inventor exclusive rights for a limited time.

questions.stem: A company has 500 old laptops to dispose of. It refurbishes 200 of them for reuse, sends 250 to an authorised recycler, and the remaining laptops go to a landfill. What percentage of the laptops is kept out of the landfill?
questions.explanation: Laptops kept out of the landfill are the refurbished ones plus the recycled ones, 200 + 250 = 450. The share is 450 / 500 x 100 = 90 percent. The remaining 50 laptops, which is 10 percent, are the ones that go to the landfill.

optionRationale.2: 50% counts only the recycled laptops (250 out of 500) and ignores the refurbished ones.
optionRationale.3: 40% counts only the refurbished laptops (200 out of 500) and ignores the recycled ones.
optionRationale.4: 10% is the share that goes to the landfill, not the share that is kept out of it.

questions.objective: Compute the share of e-waste diverted from landfill

questions.stem: Match the item in List-I with the matching example in List-II.
questions.explanation: Copyright protects a creative work such as a novel (IV). A patent protects a new invention such as an engine (III). A trademark protects a brand symbol or name (I). Presenting another person's essay as your own is plagiarism (II). The code is A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II.

optionRationale.2: This gives copyright the invention and patent the novel, which swaps the two.
optionRationale.3: This gives trademark the essay copied by a classmate and plagiarism the brand symbol.
optionRationale.4: This gives copyright the brand symbol and trademark the novel, which swaps them.

questions.objective: Match intellectual property terms with examples

right: I. The symbol and brand name of a company
II. Presenting a classmate's essay as your own work
III. A new type of engine invented by a scientist
IV. A novel written by an author
